newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia mounts search for two solo yachtsmen.
newsitem.headline: Australia mounts search for two solo yachtsmen.

text.p: Australian rescue services began an emergency search on Monday for two round-the-world yachtsmen who set off distress beacons in the Southern Ocean between Australia and Antarctica.
Officials said French yacht Amnesty International and British yacht Global Exide Challenger, competitors in the Vendee Globe race, had been hit by high seas and strong winds.

The yachts were about 1,400 nautical miles (2,600 kms) south-west of Perth, about 120 nautical miles (220 kms) further south than French yachtsman Raphael Dinelli who was rescued from his sinking yacht in freezing seas two days after Christmas.
Rescue authorities named the yachtsmen as Tony Bullimore, 56, and Frenchman Thierry Dubois, 29, who were at the rear of the field in the round-the-world race.
"I would say they are in an extreme life-threatening situation," Australian Maritime Rescue Authority spokesman David Gray told Reuters.
Australian rescue services were alerted to the emergency late on Sunday night and an airforce search aircraft was despatched from Adelaide early on Monday.
Four distress beacons had been set off and the yachts were located fairly close together, an airforce spokesman said. It was not known whether the yachtsmen had been forced to take to life rafts.
Seas were rough with a six-metre (20-foot) swell and winds of 35-40 knots.
Gray said it was the longest rescue Australian maritime authorities had attempted for a yachtsman.
Dinelli was picked up on December 27 from his half-submerged yacht Algimouss after a search aircraft dropped him a life raft and helped guide a fellow competitor to his position.
Two years ago Australian officials launched a large-scale rescue mission to save French yacthswoman Isabelle Autissier, who was competing in the same race.
